use_case_summary: Small customer support SaaS building an in-chat assistant that returns structured order updates and triggers internal tools via function calls. Primary flows: streaming assistant replies to minimize perceived latency, then a function/tool call to create orders or update tickets. Need reliable JSON-mode streaming and exact function schema enforcement so frontend validator can parse without retries.
technical_requirements: Latency target: p95 < 400ms for first token, sustained throughput ~40 concurrent lightweight chats. Cost sensitive at SMB level. Must run on public cloud hosted API initially. Expect to use function schema (tool calling) with strict JSON outputs and schema validation on client. Need audit logs and SSO integration later.
observed_issues: 1) Streams occasionally terminate with trailing commas / partial JSON fragments causing frontend parser errors. 2) Model sometimes returns 'tool_call' with name variants (e.g., 'create_order' vs 'CreateOrder') — breaks exact-match schema checks. 3) When using streaming + function mode, function arguments arrive in multiple chunks and our reassembly logic mis-detects completion boundary.
customer_quotes: 'We see about 10% of sessions fail client-side JSON validation — users get a fallback message which is bad UX.'
'When the function name casing changes it trips our router; we need deterministic tool call names.'
